title: fix(fields): a computed grid currency cell stores and shows its currency's ISO minor unit, not `scale ?? 2` (objectui#10355)
body:
Fixes #10355
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`GridField` (`@object-ui/fields`) now resolves the currency of its `currency` columns through `resolveFieldCurrency`, and gives a currency column ONE fraction width (`currencyWidth`) for both the stored value of a computed currency cell and its display: the column's authored `scale` when it has one, otherwise the resolved currency's ISO 4217 minor unit (`currencyFractionDigits`), otherwise none. The minor unit replaces only the old default of `2`.

- **`computeRow`, the stored value.** A computed `currency` cell is rounded to its authored `scale` when present. Without one it is rounded to the resolved currency's minor unit: whole yen for JPY, two places for USD, three for KWD. It no longer invents a `2`. With neither a `scale` nor a resolved currency, the value is stored as computed. `number` columns still read `scale`, unrounded when it is absent. The objectui#10071 width cap (`renderableFractionScale`) stays on the same line for both. `computeRow` takes the tenant currency as a new optional third argument.
- **`displayText`, the computed cell and the list form-factor.** A currency amount is formatted in the resolved currency at the same `currencyWidth`: `¥3,704`, `KWD 3.704`, `$1,234.57`, or `¥1,234.57` for a JPY column authored with `scale: 2`. An authored width above the engine's ceiling is clamped and reported (`renderableFractionScale`, face label `grid currency cell`, objectui#10071), since `Intl` refuses it at render. With no currency, the amount is a plain locale number with no symbol. The literal `¥` default is gone.
- **Bounded in-place fix, same file.** The editable currency cell's adornment had the same `c.prefix || '¥'` default. It now shows `c.prefix`, else the resolved currency's symbol (`currencySymbol`, the channel `CurrencyField` uses), else nothing. Left alone, the input would have shown `¥` next to a `$` display. The four conditions all hold: same defect class, a mechanical fix with a pinned shape, the file is this claim's, and the gate family is the same.
- An authored `prefix` still replaces the symbol on both faces, at the same width.
- **Comment kept true.** `percent-scale.ts`'s 「Also the NUMBER faces」 paragraph now counts three non-percent readers of a declared `scale`; the grid currency cell is the new one.
- **Rider (triage item 3).** The `PercentCellRenderer` comment in `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` now says the grid footer's **percent** arm spells `?? 0`. After objectui#10221 the currency arm reads no `scale`. One word changed.

## Why an authored `scale` still wins on a currency column (seat respin)

The first head (`69988b32e`) stopped reading `scale` on a currency column, following the triage's reading of ruling B. The seat reversed that. The spec's `InlineGridColumnSchema.scale` (objectstack `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`) still DECLARES 「Decimal places to round a computed numeric/currency result to」, and installed spec 17.4.0 accepts it on a currency inline column. Ruling B retires `FieldSchema.scale` on the currency FIELD type, a different schema. A declared key is implemented, or retired in the spec; ⛔ it is never narrowed away by its consumer. The spec half (retire inline `scale` on currency, and the stale 「(default '¥')」 `prefix` describe) is objectstack-ai/objectstack#20045.

## Reading ruling 乙 on writes (the dispatch's tension)

Ruling 乙 (objectstack-ai/objectstack#19910, comment 5805782503), item 1, verbatim: "delete `scale` on a currency field; the currency's ISO 4217 minor unit decides its display, and its write allowance stays unconstrained (today's contract)."

That "write allowance" is what the server record validator accepts. Ruling B item 4 describes it: "a currency write with more decimals than any declared precision is still ACCEPTED when nothing declares a width". Ruling 乙 says nothing about a value the client computes, so it does not forbid rounding a computed amount to the minor unit. Triage items 2 and 4 are therefore implemented as written. There is house precedent under the same ruling: `CurrencyField` (objectui#10276) already rounds typed input to the currency's minor unit on blur.

## How the currency is resolved

The call is `resolveFieldCurrency(undefined, tenantCurrency)`, and the field-level legs get nothing on purpose. No grid column declares `currency`, `currencyConfig` or `defaultCurrency`: not `GridColumn`, not `GridColumnDefinition` (`@object-ui/types`), and the spec's strict `InlineGridColumnSchema` refuses them. `deriveColumns` and `hydrateColumns` also copy none of them from the child field. Reading them off the column would add a renderer read that no authored metadata can reach. So a column's currency is the tenant default (`useLocalization().currency`), still read through the one resolver.

## Tests

Head `b229d7355` (the respin is `8fb8bc0c8`; `b229d7355` adds only the `percent-scale.ts` comment).

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/fields type-check` (dependency closure built first with `turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/fields^...'`): `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, 0 `error TS`, exit 0 at `8fb8bc0c8`.
- Pins in `packages/fields/src/widgets/GridField.currencyMinorUnit-10355.test.tsx`, 13 tests, all green at `8fb8bc0c8`:
  - storage: JPY 3 × 1234.5 stores `3704`; KWD 3 × 1.2345 stores `3.704`; the USD control stores `1234.57`; **an authored `scale` wins over the minor unit** (JPY `scale: 2` → `1234.57`, USD `scale: 0` → `1235`); with no currency the value is stored as computed; the `number` control stays unrounded.
  - display, through a real `LocalizationProvider`: a JPY edit stores whole yen and the cell shows no decimals; KWD shows three decimals; USD shows `$` on the list face and in the edit adornment, never `¥`; no currency means no symbol on either face; **an authored `scale` decides the display width** (`¥1,235` → `¥1,234.57`); **an authored `scale: 105` is clamped on the display and does not throw** (the warning names 105 and objectui#10071); an authored `prefix` replaces the symbol, not the width.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/fields/` from the repo root at `8fb8bc0c8`: 182 files passed, 1 skipped; 3073 tests passed, 7 skipped.
- The 15 suites that read `GridField.tsx` or `fields/src/index.tsx` as text: 135 passed.
- Two existing pins moved with the contract: the objectui#9909 list-mode patterns no longer expect the retired `¥`, and the objectui#10071 currency control passes `'USD'` instead of relying on the removed two-place default (12 tests, green).

## Ablations

Both legs ran through `ablation-replace.mjs` at `8fb8bc0c8`: the anchor went 1 to 0, the blob changed, and the restore was proven (blob equals HEAD `9bd016332c91`, `git diff HEAD` empty).

| Leg | Change | Result | Red | Green |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A | the old `c.scale ?? (c.type === 'currency' ? 2 : undefined)` restored in `computeRow` | 4 red, 9 green | JPY `expected 3703.5 to be 3704`, KWD `expected 3.7 to be 3.704`, no currency `expected 3.7 to be 3.7035`, JPY edit `3703.5` | the authored-scale pin, the USD and `number` controls |
| B | the authored-`scale` read removed from `currencyWidth` | 3 red, 10 green | authored-scale storage `expected 1235 to be 1234.57`, display width `expected '¥1,235' to be '¥1,234.57'`, display ceiling `expected '' to contain '105'` | the JPY and KWD no-scale pins |

## Gates (head `8fb8bc0c8`)

`check:control-bytes` OK · `check:new-line-citations` 0 new · `check-changeset-presence` passes (1 changeset: `minor` on `@object-ui/fields`).

- `check:changeset-claims`: exit 0. The 4 pending changesets that name a touched file (6625, 6694, 6837, 7166) were re-read, and all are still true.
- eslint over the 5 touched files, no inline config, JSON output: 0 errors, 165 warnings. Per-rule counts for `GridField.tsx` (27) and `index.tsx` (138) are the same as at base `778138e20`; the test files have 0.
- The gates run by the first head (`check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:doc-types`, `check:registry-bare-names`, `check:shell-escape-residue`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:esm-specifiers`, `check:self-import`, `check:phantom-deps`) passed at `69988b32e`. The respin adds no file, import or export. CI runs the full set.

## Acceptance notes

- **Spec mirror describes (filed objectstack-ai/objectstack#20045).** `InlineGridColumnSchema` (objectstack `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts`) is documented as the strict mirror of this renderer's `GridColumn`. Its `scale` describe reads "Decimal places to round a computed numeric/currency result to", and its `prefix` describe reads "Currency symbol rendered inside a `currency` cell (default '¥')". After the respin, `scale` on a currency inline column is still read, as declared. What is stale is the `¥` default, and whether the spec keeps offering `scale` on currency is the spec seat's call. Authored instances: 0. Across objectstack `examples/**`, `inlineColumns` appears in one file (the showcase invoice), and that file is identity-only. The spec half is objectstack-ai/objectstack#20045.
- **Dormant derivation gap.** A child currency field's own currency (`currencyConfig.defaultCurrency`) does not reach its grid column: the column shape has no such key, and neither derivation copies it. No master-detail child currency field in the examples declares one (invoice lines, opportunity line items), so the tenant default is correct for all of them today.
- **Docs trap (filed objectui#10406).** `content/docs/fields/grid.mdx` shows a grid column `currency: 'USD'` key that no column type declares; the spec refuses it and `GridField` never reads it.
- **Unchanged here.** The read-only table (`readonly`) prints numeric cells raw (`String(value)`). The grid's own total cell formats with no currency. Neither goes through `displayText`, and this card does not name them.
- **File surface.** The claim covers `GridField.tsx`, the tests beside it, the one `index.tsx` sentence, and one changeset. One test outside "beside" also moved: `packages/fields/src/__tests__/NumberScaleOutOfRange-10071.test.tsx`, a `computeRow` pin whose currency control encoded the removed `?? 2`. And `packages/fields/src/widgets/percent-scale.ts`, one comment sentence this PR's new reader made false, taken as a declared add-on at the seat's order.
